why: From A to B the circle and the other shape swap places. The double circle becomes a single thin circle, the thin triangle gets a thick outline, and the part of the triangle inside the circle is drawn with a double line. Do the same to C: a single thin circle at the top left, a thick pentagon at the bottom right, and the pentagon's part inside the circle drawn double. That is option 1. Option 4 has the right lines but the shapes did not swap places, and option 5 still has the double circle.
trick: In shape-swap questions, check three things: new positions, which outline became thick, and which part became double.
note: Pentagon shapes in the options are approximated from the scan; the line styles (thin, thick, double) follow the scan.
